Question: How do you think about wealth and billionaires?
Answer: “The real measure of wealth is how much you will be worth if you lost all your money” I used to think of wealth as having a million dollars in the bank, driving luxurious cars and living extravagant lives. Although most people use net worth in order to measure someone’s wealth, I have now learned to measure wealth by a different scale. First of all, wealth does not always mean having millions of dollars in your bank account. Personally, I see wealth as having a healthy body, a loving family, a great group of friends, and the freedom to live the lifestyle that I desire without having to constantly worry about money. For some, being wealthy may mean having enough passive income to pay all their monthly expenses and still have some money to spare on small luxuries at the end of the month. For others, wealth may mean $250,000 in passive income every month that will enable them to buy a luxurious mansion and travel the world 6 months out of the year. Regardless of how you currently see wealth, I encourage see it with an open mind and incorporate into your meaning the things that really matter to you the most. Do you value freedom, family time, or the status of being a multi-millionaire? If you only value the status, ask yourself the following questions: What use will having millions in the bank have for you if your body is ill with a terminal disease or if you have no one to share and enjoy your money with? These are some of the questions that I had to ask myself in my assessment of wealth and I encourage you to do the same.
